MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY AND CYTOGENETICS REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY
History of EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with disease progression on TKI therapy. Current specimen submitted for comprehensive molecular profiling and FISH analysis.

SPECIMEN TYPE
Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) - Next-Gen Precision Oncology Panel
2. Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) - RET Break Apart Analysis

MOLECULAR ANALYSIS RESULTS

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from tumor tissue and subjected to PCR amplification using the Next-Gen Precision Oncology Panel with DNA barcoding. Sequencing was performed on the GenomeSeq 500 platform. Analysis was conducted using a validated bioinformatics pipeline incorporating variant calling algorithms and clinical annotation database. The assay targets hotspot regions in the following genes:
- EGFR (exons 18-21)
- KRAS (codons 12, 13, 59, 61, 117, 146)
- NRAS (codons 12, 13, 59, 61, 146)
- BRAF (V600 region)

QUALITY METRICS
DNA concentration: Adequate
Mean coverage depth: >500x
Minimum coverage: >100x
Tumor content: Adequate for analysis

VARIANTS DETECTED

EGFR (NM_005228.5)
Variant: c.2573T>G, p.(Leu858Arg)
Location: Exon 21
Variant Allele Frequency: 39%
Clinical Significance: Pathogenic
Therapeutic Implications: Associated with sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors

KRAS: No pathogenic variants detected
NRAS: No pathogenic variants detected
BRAF: No pathogenic variants detected

FISH ANALYSIS RESULTS

METHODOLOGY
Fluorescence in situ hybridization was performed using the standard RET Break Apart FISH Probe Kit targeting the RET gene at 10q11.2. Analysis was performed according to established laboratory protocols.

RESULTS
RET (10q11.2) Break Apart FISH Analysis
Cells analyzed: 50
Cells with rearrangement: 0/50 (0%)
Result: NEGATIVE for RET rearrangement

Cutoff for positive result: ≥15% of cells with split signals

INTERPRETATION

The EGFR c.2573T>G, p.(Leu858Arg) variant detected in exon 21 at 39% allele frequency is a well-characterized activating mutation associated with increased sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC). This variant is one of the most common sensitizing EGFR mutations in NSCLC.

No additional variants with established therapeutic or prognostic implications were detected in the other genes analyzed. The absence of mutations in KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF suggests no contraindications to EGFR-targeted therapy based on this analysis.

The negative RET FISH result indicates no evidence of RET gene rearrangement, suggesting that the patient is unlikely to benefit from RET-targeted TKI therapy.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS

1. The EGFR Leu858Arg variant (exon 21) is associated with increased sensitivity to EGFR TKIs in NSCLC, including erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, and osimertinib.

2. Given the history of disease progression on TKI therapy, consideration should be given to resistance mechanisms, including potential T790M mutation (if first/second generation TKI was used) or other resistance alterations.

3. The negative RET FISH result suggests unlikely benefit from RET TKI therapy.

LIMITATIONS
- This assay detects variants in targeted regions only
- Variants below 5% allele frequency may not be detected
- Copy number variations and gene fusions (except RET by FISH) are not assessed by this panel

This report has been reviewed and electronically signed by:
[redacted name], MD, PhD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
